caps: Black pod is driven by rain.
Every year it destroys an estimated twenty to thirty percent of the world's cocoa.
The storm has just stopped.
A Malaysian smallholder has thirty minutes to scout before the disease spreads, and no way to know which block to check first.
Memory and habit are all he has.
KokoShield.
Weather-guided disease scouting.
Thirty millimetres of rain in twenty-four hours, and the system activates.
A borrowed drone marks where water is standing.
KokoShield combines that with the rain gauge, each block's drainage and past confirmed cases, and in seconds builds a thirty-minute priority route.
Block A first, then D.
He goes.
And our own Field Node, a 3D-printed sensor concept, adds local temperature and humidity at block level.
Same thirty minutes.
One scout on the usual round, one on the ranked route.
Same time, sharper path.
In the demo: fourteen suspect pods per scouting hour, against four.
Minute two, block A. Dark lesions on the lower pods.
He logs three on his phone, the adviser confirms, and only the affected blocks are treated.
Fewer pods lost to a changing climate.
Higher smallholder income.
Food systems that hold.
And the same route planner, ready for rice blast in China.
We're asking for twelve hundred ringgit to complete the first single-farm pilot.
KokoShield.
Find disease sooner after the rain.
